recognize_zh: MPO 細胞化學染色中，箭頭所指的細胞胞質布滿深藍色顆粒狀陽性反應（成熟嗜中性球，作為內部陽性對照），左下另一顆細胞亦為陽性；急性未分化白血病的母細胞應為 MPO 陰性，但本視野中陰性母細胞不明顯。
features: Arrowed cell with strong, coarse granular MPO reaction filling the cytoplasm around a pale nucleus
Second strongly positive granulocytic cell at lower left, partly obscured
Background dominated by red cells and fat spaces on a light counterstain
Few if any MPO-negative nucleated blasts clearly visible in this cropped field
Scattered fine positive granules/debris in the background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear stained for myeloperoxidase shows a mature neutrophil (arrow) with strong granular cytoplasmic positivity, serving as an internal positive control, and a second positive granulocyte at lower left. The remainder of this cropped field consists mainly of red cells and fat spaces, and MPO-negative blasts are not well demonstrated in the image. In a case of acute undifferentiated leukemia, blasts are expected to be MPO-negative (<3% positive) with no lineage-specific markers by flow cytometry. The stain is technically adequate given the positive internal control.

ddx.dx: Acute myeloid leukemia with minimal differentiation
ddx.vs: Blasts are MPO-negative by cytochemistry (<3%) but express myeloid antigens (CD13/CD33/CD117) or MPO by flow, unlike AUL.
Blasts are also MPO-negative but express CD19 with CD79a/CD22/CD10 or cytoplasmic CD3.
Blasts meet criteria for two lineages (e.g., MPO plus CD19 or cCD3), whereas AUL lacks lineage-defining markers.
